# SasaVenos Says Stimulus Recovery Adaptation Is A Cycle That Answers How Often To Train

SasaVenos says that stimulus recovery adaptation is a cycle of training, recovering, and adapting so you can train harder again, and it answers the question of how often to train. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Details

- First we train, then we recover, and then we adapt so we can train harder again. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- If you train on Monday morning, your performance might be suppressed by Wednesday evening, and that is usually the first time you can train again to present a new overload. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- You can also train on Thursday, nothing is lost. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- It is basically a combination of overload and fatigue management. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Evidence

- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "First we train, then we recover, and then we adapt so we can train harder again."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "if you do your training on Monday morning, your performance might be suppressed by Wednesday evening, and that's usually the first time you can train again to present a new overload."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "You can do it on Thursday, nothing is lost."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "It's basically a combination of overload and fatigue management. So very important."
